story_type: crew leaps from a disabled tall ship onto a motor lifeboat in heavy seas
hook: Nine crew had to leap from a tall ship onto a lifeboat.
narration: Nine crew had to leap from this tall ship onto a Coast Guard lifeboat.
The Canadian tall ship Liana's Ransom was fifty-eight miles east of Gloucester, Massachusetts.
Just after midnight, her engines quit and her sails wrapped around the mast.
Two forty-seven foot motor lifeboats came out from Station Gloucester to tow her in.
Then the seas built to nearly ten feet, and the tow line broke.
A forty-seven foot motor lifeboat can roll all the way over and right itself.
[short pause] Winds were gusting to thirty knots. Staying aboard was no longer safe.
outcome: All nine crew made it across to the Coast Guard lifeboats.
title: Leaping off a tall ship in heavy seas
description:
On March 30, 2015, Coast Guard motor lifeboat crews from Station Gloucester took nine crew off the disabled Canadian tall ship Liana's Ransom, 58 miles east of Gloucester, Massachusetts, after a tow line broke in nearly 10-foot seas.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Air Station Cape Cod, edited by Petty Officer 3rd Class Ross Ruddell, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/396880/coast-guard-rescues-nine-canadian-tall-ship
